Title: Lexar PLAY 2280 4TB M.2 NVMe SSD Review
URL: https://www.servethehome.com/lexar-play-2280-4tb-m-2-nvme-ssd-review/
Published: 2025-02-15T01:08:29.000Z
Author: Will Taillac
Highlights:
Today, we are looking at the Lexar PLAY 2280 4TB NVMe SSD. Just over a year ago I took a look at a 2230 sized drive in Lexar’s PLAY line, and today we have a more standard 2280 sized entry. Despite sharing the PLAY branding, this drive and that are very different, in more ways than just size, as you will see in my review.

...

## Lexar PLAY 2280 4TB PCIe Gen4 NVMe SSD

Beneath the included heatsink, the Lexar PLAY 2280 4TB comes in a single-sided M.2 2280 (80mm) form factor.

Lexar PLAY 2280 4TB Front

It has been a while since I have had the opportunity to complain about a drive with a difficult or impossible to remove factory heatsink; thankfully, the streak continues! The included heatsink on the PLAY 2280 has four teeny tiny screws holding it on, but after removing those it pops right off. The NAND appears to be YMTC 232-layer TLC, and the controller is a Maxio MAP1602. That combination of components makes the PLAY essentially identical to the Lexar NM790 I previously reviewed, which makes sense because they have very similar performance claims. Regardless, there is no DRAM cache.

Lexar PLAY 2280 4TB Back

The backside of the Lexar PLAY 2280 4TB has nothing of note, so the bottom of the heatsink is more interesting.

## Lexar PLAY 2280 4TB SSD Specs

The Lexar PLAY 2280 drives are available between 2GB and 8TB capacity points.

Lexar PLAY 2280 4TB Specs

All the drives in the PLAY 2280 series come rated for 7400 MB/s read and 6500 MB/s write, and those are big claims for a DRAM-less drive, pitting the PLAY 2280 against the best that Gen 4 has to offer.

Endurance is rated at 3200 TBW for the 4TB drive, which is great. My standard for endurance on a 4TB drive would normally be 2400 TBW, and the PLAY 2280 easily exceeds that. The warranty is the industry standard 5-years for a premium drive.

Lexar PLAY 2280 4TB CrystalDiskInfo

CrystalDiskInfo can give us some basic information about the SSD and confirms we are operating at PCIe 4.0 x4 speeds using NVMe 2.0.

...

Our testing uses the Lexar PLAY 2280 4TB as the boot drive for the system, installed in the M.2_1 slot on the motherboard. This slot supports up to PCIe Gen 5 x4. The drive is filled to 85% capacity with data, and then some is deleted, leaving around 60% used space on the volume.

---
